title: Nteasee: Understanding Needs in AI for Health in Africa - A Mixed-Methods Study of Expert and General Population Perspectives
measurement_description: The study evaluated general population perceptions of AI chatbot advice in healthcare by measuring how adding a religious context to a user's prompt (e.g., specifying the user is a 'Muslim woman') altered the perceived helpfulness and adherence to the chatbot's generated advice (e.g., seeking spiritual guidance). Additionally, it evaluated both expert and general population perspectives on whether religion serves as a demographic axis for AI bias and performance disparity in healthcare.
findings: When augmenting a hypothetical health chatbot's prompt with religious context (e.g., 'I am a Muslim woman'), the LLM recommended seeking spiritual guidance from an imam alongside medical advice. 45% of general population participants found this religious augmentation 'very helpful,' and seeking spiritual guidance became the next most popular intended action. Separately, experts identified religion as an axis of health inequity—noting that certain religious beliefs can act as barriers to seeking formal healthcare—and as a factor that could cause AI tools to perform differently for different groups.
